sources.title: Don MacGregor’s top tips for environmental portraiture
sources.author: Don MacGregor; reported by Jeff Kent
sources.identity: MacGregor is identified by PPA as an M.Photog., CPP, API professional portrait photographer; PPA is a professional photographers' trade association.
sources.trust_reason: First-person guidance from a named credentialed professional, published by PPA; opened full article with detailed practice discussion.
sources.notes: Specifics cover group portrait work and need adaptation before transfer to solo cosplay portraits. Article explicitly addresses composition, previsualized concept, changing field conditions, light quality, flash consistency, subject expression, explanation, and feedback.

sources.title: How to Vet a Location

sources.notes: Directly useful across woods, architecture, venues, and public locations; legal/permit details are jurisdiction-specific and should not be generalized.

gaps: No professional primary source found yet that specifically systematizes rapid portrait decisions in crowded Chinese cosplay halls, including short interactions, rapidly changing backgrounds, unobstructed working distance, and time-limited pose sequences.

Convention official policies clarify constraints but are not a unified professional method; rules vary by venue, jurisdiction, and event year. Current Japanese organizer pages should be opened and verified in Japanese in a later pass.

Field sources now cover forests/open shade, windows and workshops, architecture, twilight/night, and mixed color-temperature correction. There is still little directly opened professional teaching for exhibition halls, windowless interiors, or noisy mixed-light spaces as portrait settings.
Sequence variety appears in documentary/photojournalism sources; further independent portrait/editorial sources are needed before formalizing repeatable portrait-series coverage methods.

Chinese-language professional sources on field logistics and cosplay communication remain underrepresented; searches surfaced image galleries and event material but few accessible, attributable method sources.

Post-shoot reflection and external critique have primary professional support; on-site review cadence and a complete structured failure-checking method are still thin. A camera-specific focus-point playback guide supports only focus-point verification, not complete image quality judgment.
Location scouting evidence includes legal/accessibility/safety questions, but exact permission and publication rules require local legal/event verification and are not portable skill rules.
